body.statement: Montiel Olea, Qiu, and Stoye study randomized minimax-regret statistical treatment rules under partial identification in a finite-sample Gaussian-likelihood framework, including multiplicity of optimal rules, profiled regret, and a least-randomizing refinement.  This is the closest direct decision-theoretic antecedent.  Its cited scope is distinct from the present note's categorical-instrument joint-polytope population correspondence, moving-response-basis and moving-coefficient plug-in limit law, and exact correspondence containment.  No claim is made that the present results are the first randomized minimax-regret analysis under partial identification or that they subsume the cited paper's admissibility, profiled-regret, or least-randomizing theory.

source.locator: Abstract and opening scope paragraph, pp. 1--2
source.verbatim_statement: We do so in a finite-sample framework characterized by a Gaussian likelihood and partial identification.

attestation.note: Verified against the journal abstract and the author manuscript corresponding to arXiv:2312.17623; the abstract also records multiplicity of randomized minimax-regret rules, profiled regret, and the least-frequently-randomizing characterization.
